title: AES-128: Biased reset: numeric key example (Blömer–Seifert, FC2003)

target.description: The complete128-bit AES master key in the biased-reset concentration model.

setting.key_relation: One fixed secret master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Arbitrary key of the stated AES instance in an implementation meeting the fault and feedback assumptions.
setting.plaintext_model: Repeat the all-zero128-bit plaintext, collecting separate trials for every target key bit.

fault_model.target: State bits immediately after a selected AddRoundKey operation.
fault_model.granularity: One selected state bit per fault-injection attempt.
fault_model.timing: Precisely after the initial AddRoundKey and before first SubBytes.
fault_model.location: The attacker targets the required individual state-bit locations and can move between them.
fault_model.value_control: Known p1=3/4 for1-to0 and p0=1/4 for0-to1 changes; independent-trial concentration assumptions.
fault_model.sample_pairing: Each attempted injection yields a correct/incorrect outcome. Ciphertext-comparison feedback additionally needs a correct reference for the same input, outside the stated attempt count.
fault_model.feedback: Observable correct-versus-incorrect encryption outcome. Section1 permits alternatives: a device reset/error flag; comparison with a fault-free ciphertext; or detectable recomputation timing. Only the binary outcome is required, not the faulty ciphertext bytes.

assumptions: Successful localization and the stipulated fault-value effect are model assumptions, not measured acquisition success rates.
The ciphertext-validity alternatives are interchangeable only as a binary observation; the source does not cost each feedback channel's calibration or reference executions separately.
Recovery target: The complete128-bit AES master key in the biased-reset concentration model.

time.note: No numerical complete-attack offline runtime is reported.

data.reported: m=90112 in the whole-key example; preceding formula gives m=704 per bit
data.note: p.172 reuses the symbol m for the whole-key count.128×704=90112 reconciles the arithmetic, but the printed per-bit/total notation is retained as a conflict.

memory.note: No numerical whole-attack peak-memory budget is supplied.

preprocessing.note: No separate numerical preprocessing time is supplied.

success.description: The stated1-2^-8 is interpreted as a union-bound guarantee for128 key bits under the source model, not a physical success measurement. Printed decision-rule discrepancy remains.

evidence.interpretation: Primary-version result with explicit target, feedback model and native fault-attempt accounting; AES means128-bit blocks and the stated standard key size.

evidence.locator: Section4.1 p.171, threshold and two-hypothesis analysis
evidence.interpretation: Preserve the printed decision-rule discrepancy separately from the authors' probability-bound claim.
Full exact-edition text and AES contribution inventory reviewed; component checks and whole-attack reproduction are separate.

limitations: The paper supplies attack-model reasoning, not a physical experiment with measured chip-level success, time and calibration cost.
Attempts leaving the targeted value unchanged are informative and remain in the data budget.

field_conflicts.label: Decision rule
field_conflicts.description: The printed threshold rule guesses1 in both branches; the following analysis treats separate0/1 hypotheses. The intended complementary decision is not silently substituted.

observations.locator: Section4.1 p.171, paragraph after the threshold
observations.reported: Both the at-least-threshold and the otherwise branch are printed as guessing bit1.
Separate key-bit1 and key-bit0 error probabilities are bounded using opposite threshold events.
